q: Can a housing society get PM Surya Ghar subsidy for solar on common areas?
title: PM Surya Ghar for housing societies
short: Yes. Group housing societies and RWAs get Rs 18,000 per kW, or Rs 19,800 in special category states, for common facilities including EV charging, up to 500 kW at 3 kW per house. Individual residents' own rooftop systems count within that 500 kW limit.
audience: RWA committees and housing society managers

ul: Rate: Rs 18,000 per kW for common facilities, including EV charging.
Cap: the lower of 3 kW per house and the installed capacity, up to 500 kW in total.
The upper limit includes individual plants installed by residents in the society.
The common-facility connection must serve common facilities only, not supply residents.
100 kW with 20 houses: subsidy on 60 kW = Rs 10,80,000.
100 kW with 50 houses: subsidy on 100 kW = Rs 18,00,000.

p: Group net metering and virtual net metering installations are eligible if the system is on a roof or elevated structure and the discom approves the metering arrangement. That lets a society share solar units across connections where the state allows it.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills, including net metering lines, so grid import, export and solar generation sit in one monthly record with the factor and source shown. Figures are self-declared.
